_readme: Tables that are REAL but live on a database tools/referent_verify.py does not read.
THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST, AND IT MUST NOT BECOME ONE.
An allowlist says 'trust me'. Every entry here instead carries PROVENANCE:
the file that creates the table, and the pattern that proves the CREATE is
still in it. referent_verify re-checks that claim on every single run. If
the creating file is deleted, renamed, or has its CREATE removed, the entry
stops being evidence and the checker FAILS on the entry itself -- it does
not quietly keep passing the table.
So this file can only hold claims that are still true, and the cost of a
stale entry is a red gate, not a silent hole. That is the opposite of what
an allowlist does, and it is the only form of exception a blocking check
ADDING AN ENTRY IS NOT A WAY TO SILENCE A PHANTOM. If no file in this
repository creates the table, there is no provenance to record and the
referent is not real. Say UNRESOLVED instead.

planes.why: A standalone DuckDB file for the gate framework's own run/check/error records, deliberately separate from the write-service bus so a gate failure cannot be lost with the bus. tests/gate_framework.py writes it; tools/governor_explain.py reads it with duckdb.connect(db_path, read_only=True).

gate_checks.proof: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS gate_checks
gate_checks.note: Reported MISSING in #4080 because referent_verify's catalog covers the bus, app/models.py and migrations/ -- three planes, none of which is this file. The table is real; the plane was invisible.
